paper.title: The landscape of antibody binding affinity in SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.1 evolution
paper.supplied_bibliography_errors: None found. Crossref returns the identical title, eLife, volume 12, article e83442, 2023, and the identical nine-author list (Alief Moulana; Thomas Dupic; Angela M Phillips; Jeffrey Chang; Anne A Roffler; Allison J Greaney; Tyler N Starr; Jesse D Bloom; Michael M Desai). Crossref normalises the DOI to lower case (10.7554/elife.83442).

input_provenance.fitness_column_is: -log10(K_D,app) for binding to the named monoclonal antibody, the same quantity the paper plots as -logK_D,app. Larger = tighter antibody binding, i.e. LESS escape. Verified bit-for-bit equal to the authors' published column log10Kd in cleaned_Kds_RBD_<ab>_proper.csv (16,511 / 19,867 / 23,686 / 32,768 exact matches, zero discrepancies).
input_provenance.non_binder_handling: THIS IS THE DOMINANT PREPROCESSING CHOICE FOR THIS STUDY. Complete escapers (K_D,app above the 1 uM limit of detection) are NaN in the input and are therefore DROPPED, not censored and not imputed at the detection limit. The authors' own analyses instead retain them via a Tobit left-censored model. Consequence: the GraphFLA landscapes cover only 50.4% / 60.6% / 72.3% / 100.0% of the 32,768 genotypes for CB6 / CoV555 / REGN10987 / S309, they are NOT combinatorially complete, and any peak count or accessibility statistic computed on them is a statistic about the binder sub-landscape on a punctured hypercube. Omicron BA.1 itself is absent from three of the four landscapes.
input_provenance.unused_alternative: The authors' tables also carry log10Kd_pinned, which is identical to log10Kd for every row in all four antibodies, so it offers no censored-value alternative; a detection-limit imputation would have to be constructed from scratch (e.g. assigning -log10 K_D,app = 6 to non-binders).

overlaps.quote: Of the 32,768 variants in our library, we obtain KD, app for at least ~30,000 variants to each of the mAbs (32,603 for LY-CoV016, 31479 for REGN10987, 27485 for LY-CoV555, and 32650 for S309) after removing variants with poor titration curves (r2<0.8 or σ>1; see Methods).
overlaps.definition_quote: Paper (Methods, 'Sequence data processing'): "We then averaged the inferred KD,s values across the two replicates for each antibody after removing values with poor fit (r2<0.8 or SE>1)." plus the non-binder rule: "Variants were defined as non-binders if the difference between the maximum and the minimum of their estimated log-fluorescence over all concentrations was lower than 1 (in log-fluorescence units). This value was set by measuring the distribution for known non-binders (see Figure 1—figure supplement 1)." GraphFLA: ls.n_configs is the number of genotypes carrying a numeric fitness that survive graph construction.
overlaps.definition_divergence: The printed count includes variants whose K_D,app is ABOVE the limit of detection, i.e. complete escapers - the paper counts them as 'obtained K_D,app' because their titration is informative even though no finite K_D is fitted. In the authors' published table those genotypes carry log10Kd = NaN, so they cannot enter a GraphFLA landscape at all: a censored non-binder has no position on a -log10 K_D axis. The GraphFLA landscape therefore holds only the BINDERS.

overlaps.reason: LEAD CORRECTION: 8.586621 rounds to 8.59, not the printed 8.62, so this is not a reproduction at printed precision. The categorical part of this comparison (BA.1 is a binder for S309 and a non-binder for the other three) does reproduce exactly and is a separate, valid comparison; it must be split out before promotion. Falling within an experimental standard error is a third, different claim. The categorical half is exact: BA.1 is absent (NaN) from the CB6, CoV555 and REGN10987 inputs and present in S309, matching NB / NB / NB / binding. The numeric half is only close: the input gives -log10 K_D,app = 8.5866 for BA.1 against S309, printed 8.62 ± 0.18 - within the printed standard error but not equal. Note the same table's Wuhan Hu-1 Tite-seq values disagree with the input by more: printed 10.27 / 10.35 / 10.52 / 9.00 for LY-CoV016 / LY-CoV555 / REGN10987 / S309 against input 9.8054 / 10.1940 / 9.9593 / 9.3432. The paper does not state whether the Supplementary file 1 Tite-seq column comes from the library genotype 000000000000000 or from the separately spiked-in clonal Wuhan Hu-1 strain: NOT STATED IN PAPER. Do not use Supplementary file 1 as a per-genotype oracle.

overlaps.reason: Computed 6,333 / 32,768 = 19.33% against the printed ~17%. Variants tried, all reported: using the authors' is_clean subset only, 6,318 / 32,602 = 19.38%; using <= instead of <, 19.33%; using the Supplementary file 1 printed Tite-seq BA.1 value 8.62 as the threshold instead of the library genotype's 8.5866, 21.68%; using the isogenic value 8.81, 39.50%. The threshold that would give exactly 17% is 8.5556. No variant the paper's own stated method justifies lands on 17%; the paper's stated method (compare to BA.1's affinity) is the first one, which gives 19.3%. Recorded as a mismatch rather than tuned to fit.

overlaps.quote: We find that adding epistatic interactions improves the predictive power of the model for all four antibodies as well as for binding to ACE2, though the optimal order varies (Figure 3A). This indicates that epistasis does play a significant role in all cases (up to second order for REGN10987, to third order for LY-CoV555, and to fourth or higher order for LY-CoV016, S309, and ACE2).
overlaps.definition_quote: Paper, Methods 'Epistasis analysis': "we used a 10-fold cross-validation strategy by training each model on 90% of the dataset and examining its performance on the remaining 10%" and, for the censored measurements, "we augmented our linear model with a lower boundary, following a Tobit left-censored model (Tobin, 1958)". GraphFLA, graphfla/analysis/epistasis/higher_order.py: "Calculates the fraction of variance in fitness that can be explained by interactions between variables up to the specified order using polynomial regression", returning "The R² score representing the fraction of variance explained by polynomial terms up to the specified order".
overlaps.definition_divergence: Three independent divergences: (i) the paper's number is an argmax over orders under HELD-OUT cross-validated R2, GraphFLA's is an IN-SAMPLE R2 at a fixed order (monotone in order, so it cannot select an interior optimum); (ii) the paper fits an L2-regularised Tobit left-censored likelihood that explicitly models the non-binders, GraphFLA fits unregularised OLS on the binders only; (iii) the non-binders that the Tobit model uses are exactly the rows the GraphFLA input drops. No run was made.
overlaps.reason: The per-order R2 curve backing this sentence is plotted (Figure 3A), not printed. Its numeric backing was located in the authors' repository at desai-lab/omicron_ab_landscape data/CV_rsquared.csv and does confirm the printed ordering (mean CV R2 peaks at order 2 for REGN10987 = 0.8635, order 3 for LY-CoV555 = 0.9408, order 4 for LY-CoV016 = 0.9919 and S309 = 0.9347, order 5 for ACE2 = 0.9916), but those values are not comparable to GraphFLA's statistic for the reasons above.

verdict_reason: This paper prints no landscape-topography statistic that GraphFLA computes. An exhaustive keyword sweep of the full text and Methods returns ZERO occurrences of 'peak', 'local maximum', 'local optimum', 'ruggedness', 'sign epistasis', 'reciprocal sign', 'accessible path', 'mutational path' or 'fraction of paths'; the word 'optima' appears only as 'optimum epistasis model'. The analytical vocabulary is enrichment of escape mutations, rpart decision trees, and a Tobit-censored truncated epistasis model - none of which has a GraphFLA counterpart. The single named GraphFLA metric that comes close, higher_order_epistasis, is definition-incompatible: the paper's optimal-order statement is an argmax over 10-fold cross-validated R2 of a regularised Tobit model that explicitly uses the censored non-binders, while GraphFLA returns an in-sample OLS R2 on the binders alone. What this study DOES yield is input provenance, which was the higher-value deliverable: the four local CSVs' fitness columns are bit-for-bit identical to the authors' published -log10 K_D,app (log10Kd) columns, and the decisive preprocessing fact is that complete escapers are DROPPED rather than censored, so three of the four landscapes are punctured hypercubes covering 50-72% of the genotype space and do not even contain Omicron BA.1. Any peak count taken from them (GraphFLA gives n_lo = 100 / 391 / 174 / 210 for CB6 / CoV555 / REGN10987 / S309) is a statistic about the binder sub-landscape and has no counterpart in the paper - it must not be promoted as a literature-anchored benchmark. Two printed counts (measured-variant counts and escape fractions) could not be reconstructed exactly from the deposited tables and are recorded as mismatches with all variants tried.

lead_correction.lead_correction_2026_09_30: Corrected by the lead after external review. The original agent claim is preserved in original_agent_claim. Records are machine-consumed, so the operative field is corrected rather than only annotated.
lead_correction.population_description: The retained population is the FINITE-FITNESS subset, not a binder-only sub-landscape. The author tables keep 261 / 5,426 / 2,173 flagged non-binders with finite fitness for CB6 / CoV555 / REGN10987, so any statement in this record calling the population binder-only is wrong and must not guide preprocessing. Complete escapers above the 1 uM detection limit are NaN and therefore dropped; the authors instead retain them through a Tobit left-censored model.
